listings.title: Field Applications Engineer Intern
listings.desc:
Field Applications Engineer Intern
 Location: San Jose, California
 Employment type: U.S. internship
 Work arrangement: Fully in-office
 About the role
 As a Field Applications Engineer Intern, you will help customers and partners implement Astera Labs integrated-circuit and hardware products in real systems. You will work alongside field applications, product applications, hardware, software, validation, quality, sales, and operations teams to understand system requirements, support design-in activities, and help investigate and resolve technical issues.
 This is a hands-on opportunity to build experience across customer engineering, system-level debugging, technical communication, and product development. You will contribute to meaningful work with visible product or business impact, receive mentorship, and communicate your results to technical stakeholders.
 What you’ll do
 Learn Astera Labs products, software, and solutions and apply that knowledge to customer architectures and system requirements, including performance, workloads, software, power, thermal, and mechanical considerations.
 Support customer design-in activities, including product demonstrations, technical presentations, technical Q&A, and delivery of product and design documentation.
 Participate in customer schematic, board-layout, architecture, and system-design reviews.
 Help reproduce and understand implementation issues using system hardware details, logs, firmware and software information, operating-system details, tests, and results.
 Collaborate with product applications and other internal engineering teams to investigate issues, develop actionable solutions, and communicate next steps.
 Document customer information, debugging progress, test results, feedback, and resolution plans in Jira or related support systems.
 Assist with lab-based testing, software/firmware regressions, interoperability testing, data analysis, and technical collateral as aligned with team priorities.
 Contribute to customer-specific technical task forces and support issue transitions to the appropriate applications, engineering, or quality teams.
 Prepare clear documentation and a final presentation that explain your approach, findings, impact, and learning.
 What you bring
 Current enrollment in a bachelor’s or master’s program in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, or a related technical field.
 Strong technical fundamentals and evidence of applying them through coursework, laboratory work, research, internships, co-ops, senior design, hackathons, or personal projects.
 Interest in hardware/software systems, computer architecture, embedded systems, networking, high-performance computing, AI infrastructure, or related interconnect technologies such as PCIe or Ethernet.
 Ability to build, test, debug, analyze, and explain technical work—not simply list tools or technologies.
 Familiarity with programming or scripting, especially Python; experience with C/C++ or MATLAB is useful depending on the project.
 Systematic problem-solving skills, curiosity, attention to detail, ownership, and willingness to learn quickly.
 Clear written and verbal communication and comfort collaborating across hardware, software, validation, architecture, applications, quality, and customer teams.
 Interest in understanding customer requirements and connecting technical details to system-level outcomes.
 We value the quality, ownership, and impact of your work more than a particular school, course title, or tool list. If you meet many of the qualifications but not every item, we encourage you to apply.
 Internship experience and compensation
 This is a paid, hourly U.S. internship. The applicable hourly rate is determined as part of the offer process and specified in the offer letter, depending on education level ranges form $35/hour to $55/hour. listings.desc:
Product Applications Engineer Intern (Leo)
 Location: San Jose, California
 Employment type: Internship
 Work arrangement: On-site
 About Astera Labs
 Astera Labs builds purpose-built connectivity solutions for rack-scale AI infrastructure. The Product Applications team helps translate those products into successful system deployments through technical collateral, product integration support, lab debug, validation, and cross-functional collaboration.
 Leo is Astera Labs’ CXL Smart Memory Controller product line. Leo solutions support memory expansion, pooling, and sharing for AI and cloud platforms, with capabilities including diagnostics, telemetry, and interoperability across processor and memory ecosystems.
 The opportunity
 As a Product Applications Engineer Intern, you will work with experienced applications and engineering teams to help customers and internal partners understand, integrate, validate, and debug Leo products. You will gain hands-on experience at the intersection of high-speed connectivity, memory systems, embedded firmware/software, and customer-facing product engineering.
 This is a practical engineering role for someone who enjoys moving between technical documentation, lab investigation, data and log analysis, and collaborative problem-solving. You will contribute to meaningful work that supports products used in next-generation AI infrastructure.
 What you’ll do
 Support application-level investigation of Leo product questions and issues by reviewing system and device logs, reproducing problems in lab environments, documenting findings, and coordinating next steps with engineering teams.
 Help create, update, and review product collateral such as product briefs, datasheets, application notes, integration guidance, debug documentation, and training materials.
 Support software and firmware regression testing, including executing test flows, collecting results, identifying issues, and helping track follow-up actions.
 Participate in interoperability testing with partner devices and platforms; help analyze results and prepare clear reports for internal and external use.
 Build familiarity with CXL and PCIe-based systems, DDR memory, I2C/SMBus, embedded firmware, software development kits, diagnostics, and telemetry.
 Collaborate with Product Applications, Field Applications, firmware/software, hardware, validation, product, and sales teams throughout the product lifecycle.
 Contribute to internal product training and knowledge sharing by helping prepare materials, demonstrations, or technical walkthroughs.
 Track work and issues clearly in team tools, communicate progress and blockers, and present project outcomes to technical and business stakeholders.
 What you bring
 Currently pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in Electrical Engineering, Computer Engineering, or a related technical field.
 Coursework, project, research, or hands-on experience involving computer architecture, high-speed interfaces, memory systems, embedded systems, hardware/software integration, or system validation.
 Interest in learning how semiconductor connectivity products are integrated into real server and AI infrastructure systems.
 Ability to approach technical problems methodically, use evidence from logs or measurements, and communicate findings clearly.
 Strong written and verbal communication skills, attention to detail, and a collaborative working style.
 Experience with any of the following is helpful: C/C++, Python or other scripting, Linux, CXL, PCIe, DDR/DRAM, I2C/SMBus, firmware/SDKs, Jira, or lab equipment.
 Ability to work on-site in San Jose, California, for the internship.
 Internship experience and compensation
 This is a paid, hourly U.S. internship. The applicable hourly rate is determined as part of the offer process and specified in the offer letter, depending on education level ranges form $35/hour to $55/hour. listings.title: Product Applications Engineer Intern (Signal and Connectivity)
listings.desc:
Product Applications Intern, Signal & Connectivity (Aries/Taurus)
 Location: San Jose, California
 Employment type: Internship
 About Astera Labs
 Astera Labs is a leader in semiconductor-based connectivity solutions that enable the scalability and performance required for modern cloud and AI infrastructure. Our products help customers build high-performance, reliable systems across the data center.
 About the role
 The Product Applications Intern, Signal & Connectivity, will support product applications work across the Aries and Taurus connectivity product lines within the Signal & Connectivity Group. This role is designed for a curious, hands-on student who wants to understand how silicon, hardware, software, and customer systems come together in real-world applications.
 You will work with product applications engineers and cross-functional partners to evaluate products, investigate technical issues, support interoperability and validation activities, and turn technical findings into clear documentation. The internship offers exposure to both customer-oriented problem solving and the engineering workflows used to bring connectivity products into production.
 What you will do
 Learn the architecture, interfaces, system use cases, and application considerations for Aries and Taurus products.
 Assist with lab bring-up, product evaluation, interoperability testing, characterization, and technical debug.
 Reproduce and investigate hardware, software, firmware, and system-level issues using structured test plans and engineering data.
 Analyze logs, measurements, and test results to identify patterns, summarize findings, and recommend next steps.
 Develop or improve scripts and lightweight automation to make testing, data collection, and analysis more efficient.
 Help create and maintain application notes, test reports, debug guides, product collateral, and other technical documentation.
 Collaborate with product applications, design, firmware, validation, systems, and field-facing teams to resolve issues and support customer use cases.
 Participate in technical discussions, communicate progress clearly, and present project results to technical and non-technical audiences.
 What you bring
 Pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, or a related technical field.
 Coursework, project, laboratory, or research experience involving digital systems, computer architecture, hardware/software integration, embedded systems, or related areas.
 Interest in hands-on debugging and the ability to approach unfamiliar technical problems methodically.
 Experience with Python or another programming language for scripting, automation, or data analysis.
 Strong analytical, written, and verbal communication skills.
 Ability to work collaboratively across teams, ask thoughtful questions, and take ownership of defined projects.
 Preferred experience
 Exposure to high-speed connectivity, system interoperability, networking, or protocol-based hardware.
 Experience working with lab equipment, test automation, logs, or structured engineering data.
 Familiarity with technical documentation, issue tracking, or software repositories.
 Internship experience and compensation
 This is a paid, hourly U.S. internship. The applicable hourly rate is determined as part of the offer process and specified in the offer letter, depending on education level ranges form $35/hour to $55/hour. U.S. interns currently receive a $500-per-week housing/relocation stipend for the duration of the internship. Interns participate in Early Career programming, including technical and professional-development sessions, community events, and an end-of-program project presentation.

listings.title: Product Marketing Intern

Product Marketing Intern
 Location: San Jose, California
 Employment type: Internship

 Astera Labs is a leader in semiconductor-based connectivity solutions for cloud and AI infrastructure. The product line management organization contributes to product strategy, inbound product management, and outbound product marketing for PCIe, CXL, and Ethernet solutions.
 About the role
 As a Product Marketing Intern, you will work with product line management and cross-functional partners to understand customer needs, translate technical concepts into clear product and solution messaging, and support go-to-market execution. You will gain hands-on experience across the product life cycle while contributing to work that connects Astera Labs’ connectivity solutions with the needs of hyperscale customers and modern AI infrastructure.
 What you’ll do
 Learn how hyperscale customers use PCIe, CXL, and Ethernet connectivity solutions to build cloud and AI infrastructure, and develop an understanding of customer use cases and challenges.
 Partner with product line management, Marketing, Sales, Applications, Field Applications Engineering, Program Management, Firmware, and Product Applications teams to drive solutions and outcomes for customers.
 Develop sales-enablement collateral, product messaging, marketing slides, and other materials that communicate product value to technical and business audiences.
 Support go-to-market strategies, product positioning, industry events, web and social campaigns, and other marketing programs.
 Conduct competitive and market analysis, synthesize technical and business information, and help develop business cases.
 Support product trainings, demos, launch work, and demo messaging as assigned.
 Gather stakeholder input, set clear timelines, track deliverables, communicate progress, and keep work moving independently.
 Present findings, roadmaps, messaging, and project outcomes to cross-functional audiences.
 What you bring
 Pursuing a bachelor’s or master’s degree in engineering, business, marketing, or a related field, with an interest in product marketing, product management, semiconductors, or AI infrastructure.
 Strong written and verbal communication skills, including the ability to create clear presentations and explain complex ideas.
 Self-motivated, proactive, highly organized, and comfortable taking ownership of deliverables.
 Ability to work independently and collaboratively in a fast-moving, cross-functional environment.
 Creative, analytical, and detail-oriented approach to problem solving.
 Willingness to learn new technical and business concepts and bring forward thoughtful ideas.
 Preferred experience
 Familiarity with semiconductors, hardware and software solutions, or data-center cloud and AI infrastructure.
 Familiarity with PCIe, CXL, Ethernet, or related connectivity use cases.

 Internship experience and compensation

The applicable hourly rate is determined as part of the offer process and specified in the offer letter, depending on education level ranges form $35/hour to $55/hour. U.S. interns currently receive a $500-per-week housing/relocation stipend for the duration of the internship. Interns participate in Early Career programming, including technical and professional-development sessions, community events, and an end-of-program project presentation.

listings.desc: Overview Keysight is at the forefront of technology innovation, delivering breakthroughs and trusted insights in electronic design, simulation, prototyping, test, manufacturing, and optimization. Our ~16,800 employees create world-class solutions in communications, 5G, automotive, energy, quantum, aerospace, defense, and semiconductor markets for customers in over 100 countries. Learn more about what we do. Our award-winning culture embraces a bold vision of where technology can take us and a passion for tackling challenging problems with industry-first solutions. We believe that when people feel a sense of belonging, they can be more creative, innovative, and thrive at all points in their careers.  About Astera Labs

 As an intern, you’ll contribute to meaningful engineering projects alongside experienced professionals and gain hands-on experience with hardware that supports products from design through validation.   
 Role overview   
 As a Hardware Design Engineer Intern, you’ll join the Electrical Design team within Hardware Engineering. You’ll support the development of boards and hardware platforms used to bring up, validate, and deliver Astera Labs connectivity products.   
 This hands-on internship may include schematic design, component selection, PCB layout support, design reviews, laboratory debugging, and engineering documentation. You’ll collaborate with teams across hardware design, signal integrity, power integrity, validation, firmware, NPI, and manufacturing.   
 Responsibilities

 Team: Hardware Electrical Validation
 About the role
 Astera Labs is seeking a HW Electrical Validation Intern to help validate the hardware products that enable high-speed connectivity for AI and cloud infrastructure. In this role, you will gain hands-on lab experience with board-level validation—testing systems that incorporate Astera Labs chips—and work with hardware and ASIC designers to bring up boards, execute validation plans, analyze data, and communicate results.
 This is a practical, project-based opportunity for someone who enjoys working close to hardware, learning through measurement, and turning technical observations into clear next steps.

 Support board bring-up and initial hardware checks, including visual inspection, impedance and short checks, power-rail and voltage measurements, reference-clock checks, I²C-tree checks, and MCU firmware flashing/loading.
 Help build and execute electrical validation plans for hardware products and externally sourced hardware.
 Set up lab measurements and collect data for power, clock, and interface validation under the guidance of experienced engineers.
 Assist with power-validation activities such as noise and ripple measurements, load transients, monotonic ramp behavior, reset recovery, power sequencing, and regulator analysis.
 Use first-principles troubleshooting to investigate defined issues, document evidence, and recommend next steps.
 Analyze results and maintain clear validation records, reports, issue updates, and technical documentation.
 Collaborate with Hardware, ASIC, Firmware, System Validation, ATE, Product Applications, and manufacturing partners as needed to support bring-up and validation readiness.
 Own one scoped deliverable with visible output, such as a data package, automation script, documentation page, report update, or validation improvement.
 Share progress in team syncs and project reviews, seek feedback, and communicate blockers early.
 What we’re looking for
 Currently pursuing a degree in electrical engineering, computer engineering, or a related field.
 Hands-on academic, project, or laboratory experience with electronics, electrical measurements, or hardware debugging.
 Familiarity with core electrical concepts and a willingness to learn board-level validation methods and lab workflows.
 Strong analytical and problem-solving skills, with the ability to break down a technical problem and escalate with data.
 Clear written and verbal communication skills and a collaborative working style.
 Interest in scripting, data analysis, or automation to make validation workflows more repeatable and efficient.
 Curiosity, humility, attention to detail, and the ability to learn new tools and processes quickly.
 Internship experience and compensation
 This is a paid, hourly U.S. internship.  As a Semiconductor Packaging Intern, you will be part of the packaging team developing Astera Labs’ portfolio of connectivity products for leading cloud service providers and server and networking OEMs. You will help enhance key areas of the package development cycle, including package design, modeling, automation flows, and documentation.
 You will work cross-functionally to understand project requirements and develop solutions throughout the packaging development cycle.  Astera Labs · San Jose, CA · Internship · On-site 
 About Astera Labs
 Astera Labs builds connectivity solutions that help power modern AI infrastructure. Our products connect processors, accelerators, memory, and networks in systems where throughput, latency, bandwidth, utilization, and power efficiency directly affect customer outcomes.
 The opportunity
 Join the Performance Engineering team and help measure, understand, and improve system performance across AI and data-center workloads. You’ll work with real platforms and representative workloads to build reproducible benchmarks, analyze results, investigate bottlenecks, and communicate what the data means.
 This internship is designed for someone who enjoys combining systems knowledge, experimentation, and data analysis: define a question, design a fair test, run it repeatedly, inspect the traces and metrics, form a hypothesis, and recommend the next engineering action. You’ll work with experienced engineers on a meaningful project involving CPUs, GPUs, memory, CXL, PCIe, Ethernet, NVMe, or related connectivity systems.
 What you’ll do
 Learn the platform architecture, workload, benchmark methodology, tools, and success criteria for your assigned project.
 Design and execute reproducible performance experiments across hardware configurations, software stacks, workloads, and operating conditions.
 Measure and analyze metrics such as throughput, latency, tail latency, IOPS, memory bandwidth, GPU utilization, power, CPU utilization, and system-level performance.
 Run or support benchmark suites and workloads such as MLPerf, CXL and memory benchmarks, FIO, MLC, SPEC, database or vector-database workloads, AI inference, and custom application tests.
 Explore the performance impact of variables such as GPU count, batch size, memory placement, NUMA configuration, read/write mix, interleaving mode, link topology, and workload size.
 Capture and analyze system traces, PCIe or GPU data flows, memory behavior, logs, counters, and other evidence to identify bottlenecks and performance regressions.
 Develop Python or shell scripts to automate test execution, collect results, extract metrics from logs, convert data to analysis-ready formats, and generate plots or reports.
 Compare results across configurations, reference systems, software versions, or competitor platforms while documenting assumptions and ensuring valid comparisons.
 Investigate unexpected results by reproducing the behavior, narrowing the variables, and working with system, hardware, software, validation, and product teams to identify root causes.
 Help build repeatable performance test plans and methodologies that can be applied to new GPUs, systems, workloads, or product generations.
 Create clear technical documentation that explains the setup, workload, metrics, results, limitations, and recommendations.
 Present your project, results, and key learnings at the end of the internship.
 What you bring
 Coursework, projects, research, or hands-on experience in computer science, computer engineering, electrical engineering, data science, or a related field.
 Foundational understanding of computer architecture, operating systems, computer networks, memory systems, GPUs, storage, or distributed systems.
 Programming or scripting experience in Python, C/C++, Bash, or another language used for automation and data analysis.
 Comfort working in Linux and using command-line tools, configuration files, logs, and source control.
 Curiosity about why a system performs the way it does and a methodical approach to designing experiments and interpreting evidence.
 Ability to work with data, identify trends and anomalies, question assumptions, and communicate technical conclusions clearly.
 Ownership, persistence, and a collaborative mindset in an environment where performance questions often require iteration across multiple layers of the stack.

Physical Design Engineer Intern
 Astera Labs · San Jose, CA · Internship · On-site 
 About Astera Labs
 Astera Labs builds connectivity solutions that help power modern AI infrastructure. Our silicon teams develop complex digital products where power, performance, area, timing, physical implementation, and manufacturability must come together reliably.
 The opportunity
 Join the Physical Design team and gain hands-on experience taking a digital design from RTL handoff through physical implementation and signoff. You’ll learn how physical design methodology and flow infrastructure turn design intent into an efficient, manufacturable layout while helping improve repeatability, productivity, and design quality.
 This internship is designed for someone who enjoys both engineering fundamentals and practical problem-solving: running a flow, reading timing and QoR reports, investigating a broken stage, adjusting constraints or configuration, and measuring the effect of an iteration. You’ll work with experienced physical design, CAD, front-end, STA, EMIR, and physical-verification engineers on a meaningful project.
 What you’ll do
 Learn the physical design flow, development environment, project structure, tools, and methodology needed to contribute effectively.
 Run an assigned block through the RTL-to-signoff flow, including synthesis, floorplanning, power planning, placement, clock-tree synthesis, routing, optimization, timing closure, and signoff.
 Review physical design inputs such as RTL or netlists, SDC constraints, technology files, libraries, LEF/tech files, QRC data, and PDK-related inputs.
 Analyze timing, area, utilization, congestion, clock skew, insertion delay, transition, DRC, LVS, EMIR, and other quality-of-result reports.
 Help identify and resolve flow, implementation, timing, congestion, physical-verification, or infrastructure issues with guidance from experienced engineers.
 Support PPA exploration by running controlled experiments, comparing configurations, tracking results, and documenting the tradeoffs between power, performance, and area.
 Work with physical-design flow configuration, scripts, experiment definitions, reports, logs, and reproducible work areas.
 Contribute to CAD and flow infrastructure improvements such as report generation, run orchestration, validation checks, log mining, root-cause analysis, or handoff packaging.
 Use tools and flows such as Fusion, Innovus, PrimeTime, Calibre, Voltus, or related EDA environments under engineering guidance.
 Collaborate with front-end design, synthesis, STA, EMIR, physical verification, and other teams on inputs, handoffs, signoff criteria, and issue resolution.
 Participate in design reviews, code or flow reviews, technical discussions, issue tracking, documentation, and project planning.
 Deliver assigned physical-design work in a reproducible, well-documented state and present your project, results, and key learnings at the end of the internship.
 What you bring
 Coursework, projects, research, or hands-on experience in electrical engineering, computer engineering, computer science, VLSI, or a related field.
 Foundational understanding of digital logic, RTL, CMOS/ASIC design, computer architecture, timing, or semiconductor manufacturing.
 Interest in the physical implementation of digital designs and how layout decisions affect power, performance, area, timing, congestion, and manufacturability.
 Experience with Linux, command-line tools, source control, or scripting through coursework, projects, research, or prior experience.
 A methodical approach to debugging: understand the inputs, reproduce the issue, inspect reports and logs, test a focused change, and evaluate the result.
 Ability to learn unfamiliar tools and technical concepts, ask focused questions, communicate progress and blockers, and follow through on commitments.
 Self-motivation, professionalism, ownership, and a collaborative mindset.
 Helpful experience
 ASIC physical design, synthesis

listings.title: Signal Integrity Engineer Intern
listings.desc:
Signal Integrity Engineer Intern
 Location: San Jose, California, United States
 About the role
 Astera Labs is seeking a Signal Integrity Engineer Intern to join the Signal and Power Integrity (SI/PI) team. In this role, you will gain hands-on experience analyzing high-speed interconnects and supporting PCB- and system-level designs through simulation, measurement, and cross-functional engineering collaboration.
 You will work on a meaningful project with guidance from experienced engineers while building practical skills in signal-integrity analysis, lab validation, technical communication, and engineering judgment.
 What you will do
 Support pre-layout, layout, and post-layout signal-integrity analysis for high-speed PCB and system designs.
 Build or update simulation models and analyze critical interconnect behavior, including impedance, insertion loss, return loss, reflections, and crosstalk.
 Assist with S-parameter extraction, simulation, measurement, and interpretation for high-speed channels and differential signals.
 Support lab validation using equipment such as time-domain reflectometers, vector network analyzers, high-speed oscilloscopes, spectrum analyzers, and probing fixtures, with appropriate mentorship.
 Help plan and execute PCB/PCBA validation activities, prioritize critical items, and document results.
 Organize raw measurement data, screenshots, S-parameter files, and analysis results in project documentation.
 Collaborate with electrical, layout, validation, NPI, and other engineering partners to investigate issues and communicate findings.
 Contribute to technical reports, design reviews, and a final project presentation that explains the work, results, and impact.
 What you bring
 Enrollment in a bachelor’s, master’s, or Ph.D. program in electrical engineering, computer engineering, or a related field.
 Academic, research, or project experience with one or more of the following: high-speed digital design, signal integrity, transmission lines, electromagnetics, PCB design, differential signaling, or S-parameters.
 A foundational understanding of frequency-domain or time-domain analysis and how interconnect design affects signal quality.
 Ability to learn simulation and measurement workflows, work carefully with technical data, and communicate conclusions clearly.
 Strong ownership, curiosity, practical judgment, and willingness to collaborate across functions.
 Preferred qualifications
 Familiarity with PCB or system-level SI/PI simulation, channel analysis, or lab measurement.
 Exposure to tools or workflows used for high-speed analysis, such as ADS, HFSS, CST, Keysight, Cadence, or equivalent platforms.
 Experience with Python, MATLAB, or another scripting language for data processing and engineering analysis.
 Familiarity with calibration, de-embedding, Touchstone/S-parameter files, eye diagrams, or BER analysis.
 Internship experience and compensation
 This is a paid, hourly U.S. internship. The applicable hourly rate is determined as part of the offer process and specified in the offer letter, depending on education level ranges from $35/hour to $55/hour. U.S. interns currently receive a $500-per-week housing/relocation stipend for the duration of the internship.  Equal opportunity

listings.desc:
ABOUT US

Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies is a joint venture between two industry leaders with a clear vision for automotive’s next chapter. From operating systems to zonal controllers to cloud and connectivity solutions, we’re addressing the challenges of electric vehicles through technology that will set the standards for software-defined vehicles around the world.



The road to the future is uncharted. By combining our expertise across connectivity, AI, security and more, we’ll map a new way forward. Working together, we’ll create a future that’s more connected, more intelligent, more sustainable for everyone.



This is a general application used to fill multiple internship openings across our AI, Data, and Analytics teams. If selected, you will be matched to a specific team based on your background and interests during the interview process.

 - Data Engineering Intern - AI & Analytics

 - Data Engineering Intern - AI/ML

 - Data Engineering Intern - Analytics

 - Software Engineering Intern - AI & Machine Learning

 - Software Engineering Intern - AI Platform

 - Software Engineering Intern - DevOps

 - Software Engineering Intern - Execution Apps

 - Software Engineering Intern - Fleet Applications

 - Software Engineering Intern - Vehicle and Fleet Apps

 - Systems Analytics Engineering Intern - Connectivity and Telematics


ROLE SUMMARY

Software-defined vehicles generate enormous amounts of data, from vehicle telemetry to manufacturing and fleet operations. As a Data Engineering intern, you will help turn that data into usable, reliable infrastructure and analytics, working on data pipelines, machine learning platforms, or the software and analytics supporting fleet and manufacturing applications.

Specific project areas vary by team and may include:

 - Developing SQL and Python based data transformation and pipeline code

 - Building and maintaining ELT pipelines and analytics workflows on Databricks or similar platforms

 - Supporting machine learning model development, evaluation, or deployment infrastructure

 - Contributing to software for fleet management or manufacturing execution applications that depend on reliable data

 - Building automated data quality tests and integrating with CI/CD workflows


RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Design, build, or maintain data pipelines, analytics workflows, or ML supporting infrastructure

 - Write Python and SQL code to process, transform, and validate data

 - Collaborate with data scientists, analysts, or software engineers to meet data or platform needs

 - Contribute to automated testing for data quality and pipeline reliability

 - Document your work and share progress with your team throughout the internship


QUALIFICATIONS

Minimum:

 - Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's or Master's program at an accredited US university

 - Proficient in Python and SQL

Preferred:

 - Actively pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Mathematics, Data Science, or a closely related field, with intent to return to school after the internship

 - Coursework or project experience with data engineering, analytics, or machine learning

 - Familiarity with cloud data platforms such as Databricks, Snowflake, or Google BigQuery

 - Exposure to data transformation tools such as dbt, or infrastructure as code tools such as Terraform

 - Interest in applying data skills to vehicle, fleet, or manufacturing use cases


TOTAL REWARDS

We build the exceptional — and we believe the people doing that work should be rewarded accordingly. In addition to a competitive base salary, full-time positions may be is eligible to participate in our annual company performance bonus program. 



Payments are discretionary and not guaranteed; actual amounts depend on company results and the terms of the plan in effect, and require active employment at the time of payout. This role is also eligible for equity in the form of Restricted Stock Units (RSUs), subject to board approval and the terms of our equity incen

listings.desc:
ABOUT US

Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies is a joint venture between two industry leaders with a clear vision for automotive’s next chapter. From operating systems to zonal controllers to cloud and connectivity solutions, we’re addressing the challenges of electric vehicles through technology that will set the standards for software-defined vehicles around the world.



The road to the future is uncharted. By combining our expertise across connectivity, AI, security and more, we’ll map a new way forward. Working together, we’ll create a future that’s more connected, more intelligent, more sustainable for everyone.



Candidates should be available for a full-time commitment from January 11, 2027 to August 13, 2027.



This is a general application used to fill multiple internship openings across our Connected Systems teams. If selected, you will be matched to a specific team based on your background and interests during the interview process.

 - Connectivity Software Engineering Intern

 - Embedded Software Engineering Intern - Vehicle Access

 - Software Engineering Intern - Embedded Systems

 - Software Engineering Intern - Parallax Cloud Platform

 - Software Engineering Intern - Software Integration

 - Software Engineering Intern - Vehicle Connectivity




ROLE SUMMARY

At RV Tech, we develop next-gen vehicle features that include remote commands from mobile apps, OTA software updates, real time vehicle telemetry, and fleet management tools. All of which rely on cloud, connectivity, and integration software working together at scale. As a Connected Systems intern, you will work on the backend services, integration layers, or connectivity infrastructure that keep vehicles talking to the cloud reliably. This may involve high throughput data pipelines, distributed cloud services, or the software that validates features work end to end across the vehicle.

Specific project areas vary by team and may include:

 - Building and testing backend services that process vehicle telemetry and remote commands at fleet scale

 - Developing event driven, distributed systems using tools such as Kafka, Kinesis, or Redis

 - Contributing to cross domain systems integration and validation work, ensuring vehicle features function correctly end to end

 - Supporting connectivity infrastructure, including the messaging and communication layers linking vehicle, mobile app, and cloud

 - Working with cloud native infrastructure on AWS (EKS, Lambda, DynamoDB, IoT Core)


RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Design, develop, and test software components within an existing distributed or connectivity system

 - Write clean, maintainable code in Python, Go, C++, or Java depending on the team

 - Participate in code reviews, design discussions, and debugging sessions with your team

 - Contribute to test automation and validation for integration or connectivity features

 - Document your work and present progress to your team throughout the internship


QUALIFICATIONS

Minimum:

 - Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's or Master's program at an accredited US university

 - Proficient in at least one of Python, Go, C++, or Java

Preferred:

 - Actively pursuing a degree in Computer Science, Computer Engineering, Electrical Engineering, or a closely related field, with intent to return to school after the internship

 - Exposure to distributed systems, event driven architecture, or cloud platforms, AWS preferred

 - Familiarity with vehicle communication protocols such as CAN or MQTT, or IoT concepts

 - Coursework or project experience with backend development, systems integration, or test automation


TOTAL REWARDS

We build the exceptional — and we believe the people doing that work should be rewarded accordingly. In addition to a competitive base salary, full-time positions may be is eligible to participate in our annual company performance bonus program. 



Payments are discretionary and not guaranteed; actual amounts depend on company results and the term

When software-defined vehicles accelerate, manage battery temperature during fast charge, activate body controls, respond to steering input, or detect a system fault, the embedded software making that possible was built by a vehicle controls team. As a Vehicle Controls intern, you will work on embedded software or controls algorithms for one of several vehicle domains, including propulsion and dynamics, energy storage and charging, thermal and HVAC systems, body controls, functional safety, or systems engineering and test automation supporting these domains.

Specific project areas vary by team and may include:

 - Implementing and validating embedded software for battery management, charging, or energy distribution systems

 - Developing controls software for thermal and HVAC systems, body controls, or lighting

RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Communicate progress and technical tradeoffs to your team throughout the internship

 - Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's or Master's program at an accredited US university

 - Proficiency in C or C++, with some exposure to Python

 - Actively pursuing a degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Computer Science, or a closely related field, with intent to return to school after the internship

 What if your next project helped power the future of technology? 
 At Intel, you'll do more than learn, you'll contribute. You’ll work side-by-side with industry leaders, gain hands-on experience on meaningful projects, and help solve real-world challenges that affect billions of people worldwide. From advanced semiconductor manufacturing to AI-powered innovations, you'll play a role in technologies that redefine how the world works, learns, and connects.
 What makes Intel unique is the opportunity to see the entire technology lifecycle in action. Unlike many companies where hardware, software, and manufacturing operate separately, Intel brings them together, giving you exposure to everything from research and design to advanced semiconductor manufacturing and global deployment.
 Whether you're tackling engineering challenges, improving operations, analyzing data, advancing next-generation technologies, or supporting global customers, you'll build valuable skills while contributing to innovations that enable a more sustainable and connected future.
 Bring your curiosity, make an impact, and see where your ideas can take you at Intel. 
 What You'll Do 
 Build technologies that power the future of computing. As a Silicon Hardware Engineering Intern, you'll work on meaningful projects while building technical expertise that accelerates your professional growth.
 Silicon architecture, circuit design, logic, layout, physical design, verification, validation, and debug.
 Design, build, test, and analyze technologies at the core of Intel processors and platforms.
 Use scripting, data analysis, and hardware validation methods to solve technical problems.
 Collaborate across silicon, product, and manufacturing teams.
 Contribute to innovations in processors, GPUs, SoCs, photonics, and validation systems.
 Develop technical depth, tackle complex challenges, and contribute from day one while learning alongside experienced Intel engineers and technical leaders.
 Where Your Career Could Take You 
 Potential opportunity areas include:
 Analog Circuit Design Engineer
 CPU/GPU Design Verification Engineer
 GPU Physical Design Engineer
 DFT Design Engineer
 Formal Verification Engineer
 Product Development Engineer
 Product Failure Analysis Engineer
 Silicon Product Architect
 SoC Logic Design Engineer
 Build technical expertise, explore new possibilities, and help shape what is next in computing and semiconductor technology.
 Qualifications: 
 Must possess the minimum qualifications below to be initially considered for this position. Experience may be gained through coursework, research, academic projects, internships, laboratory work, student organizations, leadership experiences, or other relevant experiences.
 Minimum Qualifications 
 Currently pursuing a Bachelor’s degree in Computer Engineering, Computer Science, Electrical Engineering, Physics, or a related STEM field.
 3+ months of experience gained through coursework, academic projects, research, internships, co-ops, student organizations, assistantships, or other relevant technical experiences.
 Preferred Qualifications 
 GPA of 3.0 or higher preferred.
 Experience or interest in design, architecture, programming, scripting, data analysis, automation, modeling, simulation, validation, or debugging.
 Hands-on coursework, research, projects, or internship experience related to the role family.
 Strong problem-solving, communication, collaboration, and ability to work in team-based environments.

listings.desc:
ABOUT US

Rivian and Volkswagen Group Technologies is a joint venture between two industry leaders with a clear vision for automotive’s next chapter. From operating systems to zonal controllers to cloud and connectivity solutions, we’re addressing the challenges of electric vehicles through technology that will set the standards for software-defined vehicles around the world.



The road to the future is uncharted. By combining our expertise across connectivity, AI, security and more, we’ll map a new way forward. Working together, we’ll create a future that’s more connected, more intelligent, more sustainable for everyone.



This is a general application used to fill multiple internship openings across our Electrical Hardware teams. If selected, you will be matched to a specific team based on your background and interests during the interview process.

 - Electrical Design Engineering Intern

 - Electrical Engineering Design Intern

 - Electrical Functional Safety Engineering Intern

 - Embedded Software Engineering Intern

 - Mechanical Design Engineering Intern

 - Product Launch Engineering Intern

 - Reliability Engineering Intern

 - Software Engineering Intern - Vehicle Lab

 - Supplier Excellence Engineering Intern

 - Test Automation Systems Engineering Intern




ROLE SUMMARY

Every Electronic Control Unit goes through a full lifecycle of design, validation, manufacturing readiness, and release. As an Electromechanical Design Engineering intern, you will be involved in one part of that lifecycle, which may include circuit design, mechanical packaging, hardware validation and test, reliability and functional safety analysis, or supplier and manufacturing readiness work.

Specific project areas vary by team and may include:

 - Designing and developing analog, digital, or mixed signal circuits, including schematic capture and component selection

 - Supporting mechanical packaging design or structural and thermal simulation for ECU enclosures

 - Building or running hardware validation tests and test automation systems

 - Contributing to hardware functional safety analyses such as FMEA or FMEDA

 - Supporting supplier quality, product launch, or manufacturing readiness activities for ECU programs


RESPONSIBILITIES

 - Support proof of concept, design, or validation work for an assigned hardware project

 - Debug and troubleshoot hardware issues at the board or system level

 - Document component release information and maintain accurate design records

 - Collaborate with cross functional engineering and design teams to understand requirements

 - Communicate progress and findings to your team throughout the internship


QUALIFICATIONS

Minimum:

 - Currently enrolled in a Bachelor's or Master's program at an accredited US university

 - Proficient in electrical engineering fundamentals

Preferred:

 - Actively pursuing a degree in Electrical Engineering, Mechanical Engineering, Hardware Engineering, or a closely related field, with intent to return to school after the internship

 - Understanding of electronics, packaging, and hardware design

 - Familiarity with communication protocols such as CAN, Ethernet, USB, I2C, or SPI

 - Coursework or project experience with PCB design tools, CAD tools, or simulation software

listings.title: Digital Design Engineering Intern
listings.desc:
Change the world. Love your job.  
 About TI: 
Texas Instruments Incorporated (TI) is a global semiconductor design and manufacturing company that develops analog ICs and embedded processors. By employing the world’s brightest minds, TI creates innovations that shape the future of technology. TI is helping about 100,000 customers transform the future, today. We’re committed to building a better future – from the responsible manufacturing of our semiconductors, to caring for our employees, to giving back inside our communities and developing great minds. Put your talent to work with us – change the world, love your job!
 About the job: 
In this position, you will be working on low-power RF communication circuits and IoT devices using state-of-the art process technology. You will be creating specific circuitry for modulation and demodulation of information into RF signals, as well as other aspects related to low power radio communication.
Your responsibilities will include RTL coding, simulation, synthesis, verification and debugging of communication chips both at the circuit level and behavioral level. You will be able to define and test new modulation and demodulation algorithms for different modulation formats like BPSK, FSK, QAM and OFDM. You will develop those algorithms using low-level embedded assembler-programmed CPUs. You will participate in the development of new low-power architectures for future products.
 This position involves routine communication with a highly talented team of analog and digital design engineers to solve problems and present information as well as active participation in work groups, providing ideas and collaborative teamwork.
 Minimum requirements:  
 MSc Degree in Electronics Engineering, Telecommunication Engineering, or related field.
 1-3 years of relevant experience. Exceptional newly graduated candidates will be also considered.
 Good knowledge of communication theory and digital signal processing
 Understanding of digital logic design 
 Familiarity with the Verilog and VHDL language and simulators 
 Strong programming skills: Matlab, C, Python and Assembler
 Understanding of analog and RF electronics and exposure to analog IC design methods 
 Excellent communication skills in English
 Preferred qualifications:  
 Ability to solve problems using a systematic approach
 Strong verbal and written communication skills 
 Ability to work in teams and collaborate effectively with people in different functions 
 Strong time management skills that enable on-time project delivery 
 Demonstrated ability to build strong, influential relationships 
 Ability to work effectively in a fast-paced and rapidly changing environment 
 Ability to take the initiative and drive for results
 Our offer for you: 
 Benefit from an attractive compensation  
 Join an international work environment where your ideas count and where you can thrive in a diverse culture  
 Explore a world of opportunities for your personal and professional development 
To be considered for this position, please apply.

- Experience in designing power delivery circuits in advanced silicon process taking from circuit to layout to silicon prototype is highly desirable.
- Familiarity with post-silicon verification methods, including testing and characterization techniques.
